The following text is from Charlotte Brontë's 1847 novel *Jane Eyre*. The narrator, Jane, is a young girl living with her aunt, Mrs. Reed.

There was no possibility of taking a walk that day. We had been wandering, indeed, in the leafless shrubbery an hour in the morning; but since dinner (Mrs. Reed, when there was no company, dined early) the cold winter wind had brought with it clouds so sombre, and a rain so ______, that further outdoor exercise was now out of the question. I was glad of it: I never liked long walks, especially on chilly afternoons.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The rain, together with the cold wind and gloomy clouds, made outdoor exercise “out of the question,” so it must have been heavy and soaking enough to get through clothing. “Penetrating” (piercing, soaking through) fits this meaning.

Choice A is wrong because a “gentle” rain would not make a walk impossible. Choice C is wrong because the rain is described alongside a “cold winter wind” and “sombre” clouds as something that ruled out going outside, not as something pleasant. Choice D is wrong because a “brief” rain would not keep the family indoors for the rest of the afternoon.
explanation_uz:
Yomg‘ir sovuq qishki shamol va qovog‘i soliq bulutlar bilan birga tashqarida sayr qilishni butunlay imkonsiz qilib qo‘ygan (“out of the question”). Demak, yomg‘ir kiyimdan o‘tib ketadigan darajada kuchli va zax bo‘lgan. “Penetrating” (ichiga o‘tib ketadigan, suyak-suyakka o‘tadigan) so‘zi shu ma’noga mos keladi.

A noto‘g‘ri: “gentle” (mayin) yomg‘ir sayrni imkonsiz qilmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: yomg‘ir sovuq shamol va “sombre” (qorong‘i, g‘amgin) bulutlar qatorida tilga olinadi, ya’ni u yoqimli narsa sifatida emas, tashqariga chiqishga to‘sqinlik qilgan narsa sifatida tasvirlangan. D noto‘g‘ri: “brief” (qisqa) yomg‘ir oilani butun kun davomida uyda ushlab turmas edi.

The following text is from Willa Cather's 1913 novel *O Pioneers!*

One January day, thirty years ago, the little town of Hanover, anchored on a windy Nebraska tableland, was trying not to be blown away. A mist of fine snowflakes was curling and eddying about the cluster of low drab buildings huddled on the gray prairie, under a gray sky. The dwelling-houses were set about haphazard on the tough prairie sod; some of them looked as if they had been moved in overnight, and others as if they were straying off by themselves, headed straight for the open plain. None of them had any appearance of ______, and the howling wind blew under them as well as over them.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The houses look as if they “had been moved in overnight” or were “straying off by themselves,” and the wind blows even under them. In other words, none of them looks settled or lasting. “Permanence” (the quality of lasting or staying in place) completes the description logically.

Choice A is wrong because nothing in the text concerns festivity; the description is about how unsettled the houses look. Choice B is wrong because the houses are “set about haphazard,” so they clearly do look disordered. Choice C is wrong because houses that seem to be “straying off” and “headed straight for the open plain” do give an appearance of movement.
explanation_uz:
Uylar go‘yo “bir kechada ko‘chirib keltirilgan” yoki “o‘z-o‘zidan dashtga qarab ketib qolayotgan”dek ko‘rinadi, shamol esa hatto ularning tagidan ham esadi. Boshqacha aytganda, birortasi ham mustahkam, uzoq turadigan joyga o‘xshamaydi. “Permanence” (doimiylik, mustahkam turib qolish) so‘zi tasvirni mantiqan to‘ldiradi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda bayram yoki shodlik haqida gap yo‘q, tasvir uylarning beqarorligi haqida. B noto‘g‘ri: uylar “haphazard” (tartibsiz) joylashgan, demak ular tartibsiz ko‘rinadi — bu jumlaga zid. C noto‘g‘ri: “ketib qolayotgan” va “dashtga qarab yo‘l olgan”dek ko‘ringan uylar aynan harakatdagidek taassurot qoldiradi.

passage: The new footbridge over the canal in the town of Nurobod was designed in lightweight sections so that it could be ______ quickly. Workers put the entire structure together in a single weekend, and the road beside the canal had to be closed for only a few hours.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The second sentence explains what happened quickly: workers “put the entire structure together in a single weekend.” A word meaning “put together” is needed, so “assembled” is correct.

Choice A is wrong because the text is about how the bridge was built, not about people's opinions of it. Choice B is wrong because nothing suggests the bridge was left unused. Choice D is wrong because measuring the bridge is not the same as putting it together, which is what the workers did in one weekend.
explanation_uz:
Ikkinchi jumla nima tez bajarilganini tushuntiradi: ishchilar “butun inshootni bitta dam olish kunlarida yig‘ib qo‘yishgan.” Demak, “yig‘moq” ma’nosidagi so‘z kerak — “assembled” to‘g‘ri javob.

A noto‘g‘ri: matn ko‘prikka odamlarning munosabati haqida emas, uning qanday qurilgani haqida. B noto‘g‘ri: ko‘prik tashlab qo‘yilgani haqida hech qanday ishora yo‘q. D noto‘g‘ri: ko‘prikni o‘lchash uni yig‘ish bilan bir xil emas, ishchilar esa aynan uni bir dam olish kunida yig‘ishgan.

The following text is from Mark Twain's 1883 memoir *Life on the Mississippi*. Twain recalls the town on the Mississippi River where he grew up. A “packet” is a steamboat that carries passengers and goods on a regular route.

Once a day a cheap, gaudy packet arrived upward from St. Louis, and another downward from Keokuk. Before these events, the day was glorious with ______; after them, the day was a dead and empty thing. Not only the boys, but the whole village, felt this. After all these years I can picture that old time to myself now, just as it was then: the white town drowsing in the sunshine of a summer's morning; the streets empty, or pretty nearly so; one or two clerks sitting in front of the Water Street stores, with their splint-bottomed chairs tilted back against the wall, chins on breasts, hats slouched over their faces, asleep…
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The sentence contrasts the time before the boats arrived with the time after: afterward the day was “dead and empty.” Before the arrivals, then, the day must have been full of something positive that the boats' arrival used up. “Expectancy” (eager waiting for something to happen) fits: the day was “glorious” because everyone was looking forward to the boats.

Choice B is wrong because “regret” is a negative feeling about something past and could not make a day “glorious.” Choice C is wrong because ordinary “routine” would not be called glorious, and it does not explain why the day became empty once the boats had come. Choice D is wrong because “exhaustion” is negative and does not contrast with the “dead and empty” day that followed.
explanation_uz:
Jumla kemalar kelishidan oldingi va keyingi vaqtni qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi: keyin kun “o‘lik va bo‘m-bo‘sh” bo‘lib qolgan. Demak, kemalar kelishidan oldin kun qandaydir ijobiy narsa bilan to‘la bo‘lgan va kemalar kelishi bilan bu narsa tugagan. “Expectancy” (biror narsani intiqlik bilan kutish) mos keladi: hamma kemalarni kutgani uchun kun “ajoyib” (glorious) bo‘lgan.

B noto‘g‘ri: “regret” (afsus) — o‘tgan narsa haqidagi salbiy tuyg‘u, u kunni “ajoyib” qila olmaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: oddiy “routine” (odatiy tartib) ajoyib deb atalmaydi va nima uchun kemalar kelgach kun bo‘shab qolganini tushuntirmaydi. D noto‘g‘ri: “exhaustion” (holdan toyish) salbiy ma’noli va keyingi “o‘lik va bo‘sh” kunga qarama-qarshi qo‘yilmaydi.

The following text is from Frederick Douglass's 1845 autobiography *Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave*.

I have no accurate knowledge of my age, never having seen any authentic record containing it. … A want of information concerning my own was a source of unhappiness to me even during childhood. The white children could tell their ages. I could not tell why I ought to be deprived of the same privilege. I was not allowed to make any inquiries of my master concerning it. He deemed all such inquiries on the part of a slave improper and ______, and evidence of a restless spirit.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Douglass was “not allowed” to ask about his age, and his master considered such questions “improper” and a sign of “a restless spirit.” The missing word must be another disapproving term that fits beside “improper.” “Impertinent” (rude, disrespectful, overstepping one's place) is the precise choice.

Choice A is wrong because the master forbade the questions, so he clearly did not think them “harmless.” Choice B is wrong because “admirable” is praise, which contradicts “improper.” Choice D is wrong because “customary” means usual or expected, yet the master forbade these questions, and Douglass notes that enslaved people generally did not know their birthdays.
explanation_uz:
Duglasga o‘z yoshi haqida so‘rashga “ruxsat berilmagan,” xo‘jayini esa bunday savollarni “improper” (nojo‘ya) va “bezovta ruh”ning belgisi deb hisoblagan. Bo‘sh joyga “improper” yonida turadigan yana bir qoralovchi so‘z kerak. “Impertinent” (beadab, o‘z haddidan oshgan) — aniq tanlov.

A noto‘g‘ri: xo‘jayin bu savollarni taqiqlagan, demak ularni “harmless” (zararsiz) deb hisoblamagan. B noto‘g‘ri: “admirable” (tahsinga loyiq) — maqtov, bu “improper” so‘ziga zid. D noto‘g‘ri: “customary” odatiy, kutilgan degani, ammo xo‘jayin bu savollarni taqiqlagan, Duglas esa qullar odatda tug‘ilgan kunini bilmasligini aytadi.

passage: Botanist Shirin Qodirova expected the seeds of the desert shrub she studies to sprout as soon as they were watered in her laboratory. Instead, the seeds remained ______ for nearly four months, showing no sign of growth until they had been exposed to a series of cold nights. Qodirova suspects that this delay keeps the young plants from sprouting in autumn, only to be killed by winter frost.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
The seeds showed “no sign of growth” for months until a period of cold nights, even though they had water. A word describing a resting, inactive state is needed. “Dormant” (alive but temporarily inactive) fits precisely.

Choice A is wrong because the text says nothing about the seeds breaking easily; it describes their failure to grow. Choice B is wrong because “abundant” refers to quantity, and the number of seeds is irrelevant to the delay. Choice C is wrong because whether the seeds could be seen has nothing to do with their not sprouting.
explanation_uz:
Urug‘lar suv berilganiga qaramay, bir necha oy davomida sovuq kechalar o‘tmaguncha “o‘sish belgisini ko‘rsatmagan.” Demak, tinch, faol bo‘lmagan holatni bildiruvchi so‘z kerak. “Dormant” (tirik, lekin vaqtincha harakatsiz, uyqudagi) aynan shu ma’noni beradi.

A noto‘g‘ri: matnda urug‘larning tez sinishi haqida gap yo‘q, ularning o‘smagani haqida gap boradi. B noto‘g‘ri: “abundant” (mo‘l) miqdorni bildiradi, urug‘lar soni esa kechikishga aloqasi yo‘q. C noto‘g‘ri: urug‘larning ko‘rinishi yoki ko‘rinmasligi ularning unib chiqmaganiga aloqador emas.

passage:
The following text is from Jane Austen's 1813 novel *Pride and Prejudice*. The narrator describes Mr. and Mrs. Bennet.

Mr. Bennet was so odd a mixture of quick parts, sarcastic humour, reserve, and caprice, that the experience of three-and-twenty years had been insufficient to make his wife understand his character. Her mind was less difficult to develope. She was a woman of ______ understanding, little information, and uncertain temper. When she was discontented, she fancied herself nervous. The business of her life was to get her daughters married: its solace was visiting and news.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Mr. Bennet is too complicated for his wife to understand, but “her mind was less difficult to develope” (that is, to figure out), and she has “little information.” The missing word must describe a limited, unremarkable intelligence. “Mean” is correct here in its older sense of “inferior” or “of low quality” (not “unkind”): she was a woman of limited understanding.

Choice B is wrong because a “keen” (sharp) understanding contradicts the claim that her mind was simple and that she could not understand her husband. Choice C is wrong for the same reason: “profound” means deep. Choice D is wrong because the text says her mind was “less difficult” to figure out than her husband's, so it was not “mysterious.”
explanation_uz:
Janob Bennet xotini tushuna olmaydigan darajada murakkab odam, ammo xonimning “aqlini tushunish ancha oson edi” (“less difficult to develope”), bundan tashqari u “kam ma’lumotli” edi. Demak, bo‘sh joyga cheklangan, oddiy aql-idrokni tasvirlovchi so‘z kerak. “Mean” bu yerda eski ma’nosida — “past, pastroq sifatli” degan ma’noda keladi (“yovuz” ma’nosida emas): u aql-idroki cheklangan ayol edi.

B noto‘g‘ri: “keen” (o‘tkir) aql uning ongi oddiy ekani va erini tushuna olmasligiga zid. C ham shu sababli noto‘g‘ri: “profound” — chuqur degani. D noto‘g‘ri: matnda uning ongini tushunish eriga qaraganda “osonroq” ekani aytilgan, demak u “mysterious” (sirli) emas.

passage:
The following text is from Henry David Thoreau's 1862 essay “Walking.” Thoreau has been discussing two possible origins of the word “saunterer,” meaning a person who walks at a leisurely pace.

Some, however, would derive the word from sans terre without land or a home, which, therefore, in the good sense, will mean, having no particular home, but equally at home everywhere. For this is the secret of successful sauntering. He who sits still in a house all the time may be the greatest vagrant of all; but the saunterer, in the good sense, is no more vagrant than the meandering river, which is all the while ______ seeking the shortest course to the sea.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation_en:
Thoreau argues that the saunterer is “no more vagrant” (aimless) than a river. Although a river “meanders,” it is always heading toward a goal, “the shortest course to the sea.” The missing word must therefore stress purposeful, persistent effort. “Sedulously” (diligently, with steady attention) conveys this.

Choices A and D are wrong because “idly” and “randomly” would make the river aimless, which is exactly what Thoreau denies when he says it is no more vagrant than the saunterer and is seeking “the shortest course.” Choice C is wrong because nothing suggests the river is unwilling; the comparison is about direction and purpose, not reluctance.
explanation_uz:
Toro sayr qiluvchi (saunterer) daryodan ortiq “daydi” (maqsadsiz) emasligini ta’kidlaydi. Daryo garchi ilon izi bo‘lib oqsa ham, doim bir maqsad sari — “dengizga eng qisqa yo‘l” sari intiladi. Demak, bo‘sh joyga maqsadli, tinimsiz harakatni ta’kidlovchi so‘z kerak. “Sedulously” (tirishqoqlik bilan, tinmay, astoydil) shu ma’noni beradi.

A va D noto‘g‘ri: “idly” (bekorchilik bilan) va “randomly” (tasodifiy) daryoni maqsadsiz qilib qo‘yadi, Toro esa aynan buni inkor etadi — daryo “eng qisqa yo‘l”ni izlaydi. C noto‘g‘ri: daryo istamay harakat qilayotgani haqida hech qanday ishora yo‘q; taqqoslash yo‘nalish va maqsad haqida, istamaslik haqida emas.
